transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you saw a problem that wasn't yours to fix, and you fixed it anyway.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: Our staging environment kept failing Fridays. It was the infra team's domain. I looked into cron logs, found a memory leak in the report generator, patched it, and it stopped failing. My manager was happy.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate on a technical decision.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: My teammate wanted GraphQL for our admin API and I thought REST was simpler. I wrote a comparison doc and we had a call. We went with REST with a plan to revisit.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you were wrong about something technical.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I was convinced optimistic locking was right for our cart service. After a production incident, I dug in and realized we needed pessimistic locking. I updated the implementation and bugs stopped.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: What's a weakness you've had to actively work on?

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: I used to give feedback that landed as harsh. A colleague told me directly. I've been framing feedback as questions rather than statements.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Tell me about a time you had to push back on a direction you disagreed with.

transcript.speaker: candidate
transcript.text: The PM wanted to ship behind a feature flag permanently. I sent an estimate of maintenance cost. We compromised on a six-week cleanup window.
